name: MKI Screen Fit
overview: Full HD screens play the Full HD version, and transcodes stay no larger than the screen.
description: When a movie has a 4K and a Full HD version (for example merged by MKI Merge Versions) and someone starts it on a screen that cannot show more than Full HD, the Full HD file plays instead: no transcode of a 4K file for a laptop. Only when both versions are the same cut and the Full HD one has the chosen audio and subtitle language, and never when someone picked a version by hand. Optionally, a transcode that has to re-encode the video anyway (unsupported codec or HDR, burned-in subtitles, a bitrate limit) is kept no larger than the screen. Browsers and the Jellyfin apps built on the web client measure their screen; for TV apps you choose per device. Bitrate limits, transcode throttling, direct play and remuxing stay exactly as Jellyfin decides. Everything starts turned off.
changelog: First release. Plays the Full HD version of a movie with several versions on screens up to 1200 pixels tall, and can keep re-encoded transcodes no larger than the screen. Browsers and the Jellyfin apps built on the web client report their screen; TV apps can be set per device on the settings page, which also lists recent decisions. Everything starts turned off.
